text:
maria: FYI customer behind enterprise proxy reporting intermittent 502/SSL errors when calling hosted API. They say app uses HTTP CONNECT to tunnel 443 but TLS handshake fails after proxy upgrade. Logs attached by customer show cert name mismatch and we see CONNECT rewritten sometimes.

alex: can you paste the exact curl they used and the error? also which region/model/endpoint?

maria: region=us-west-2, endpoint=https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate, model=gpt-4o-mini. Customer repro from their app: 
```
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" 
```
Response: TLS handshake: "certificate subjectAltName does not match target host name 'api.redwood.ai'" and sometimes HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway.

julie: that sounds like a TLS intercepting proxy doing MITM (terminating TLS and reissuing). For CONNECT tunnels proxies normally shouldn't tamper with SNI, but some appliance 'inspectors' will terminate and reissue certs. If they reissue with CN=corp-proxy.corp you'll get name mismatch unless they inject their root CA into the client truststore.

maria: customer says they don't have the org CA installed on some hosts — but curious bit: tcpdump from a failing host shows ClientHello SNI "api.redwood.ai" but server cert presented is "lb-internal.corp". So it looks like the proxy is rewriting the SNI or doing selective interception then forwarding to an internal load balancer that returns a different cert.

alex: could be two things: 1) proxy is intercepting and re-signing (requires CA on client), 2) proxy is doing CONNECT to a different upstream host (host header/SNI rewrite) because of allowlist or hostmap (eg they map api.redwood.ai -> internal proxy target). We should ask for a pcap showing the CONNECT request and the TLS ClientHello bytes.

maria: asked customer to capture; they provided a small pcap snippet and the browser curl -v. In pcap I can see: 
- TCP stream: client -> proxy: "CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1"
- proxy -> upstream: "CONNECT lb-internal.corp:443 HTTP/1.1"
so proxy is rewriting the CONNECT target.

julie: aha that explains the cert mismatch. If proxy rewrites the CONNECT host then the upstream receives SNI for lb-internal.corp (or the proxy re-initiates TLS), resulting in the LB cert. Ask customer if their proxy uses a hostmap/egress allowlist or split DNS (internal DNS resolving api.redwood.ai to internal IP).

maria: customer says they have split-horizon DNS + proxy rules. Quick support checklist I'm proposing: 
1) capture full tcpdump of failed flow (sudo tcpdump -i any host api.redwood.ai and port 443 -w capture.pcap)
2) capture the plaintext CONNECT headers (curl -v) and the proxy's upstream CONNECT (if visible)
3) if proxy is intercepting, either install corp CA into app truststore or configure proxy to tunnel (no TLS inspection) for api.redwood.ai
4) alternatively, allowlist our egress IP ranges so proxy doesn't rewrite target (we provide ranges/hostnames in docs).

alex: add to that: request proxy vendor and version, and whether they're using explicit MITM or a forward proxy + egress nat. Also request whether the app uses system truststore or bundled truststore (some apps embed certs so interception still fails).

maria: customer replied: app is Java 11 using default truststore for many hosts; their corporate security won't add our root CA. They prefer not to change trust stores. They asked if we can provide an alternate endpoint or IP they can allowlist that will preserve SNI.

julie: short term we can suggest they allowlist our egress IP range for us-west-2 and ensure the proxy is configured to tunnel CONNECT for that range. Long term, we should document recommended proxy configs in Private/VPC guide (allowlist by destination IP, or enable passthrough for CONNECT to api.redwood.ai).

maria: I've given them our published egress IP list and a sample proxy rule: 
```
# example squid acl to bypass MITM for our API
acl redwood dst 34.120.23.0/24 34.120.24.0/24
cache_peer_access parental deny redwood
never_direct allow redwood
```
(we should verify exact CIDRs in docs; I used placeholders).

alex: also note: some proxies still rewrite the CONNECT target even for IP allowlist if internal host mapping exists. Ask them to show proxy config (NAT/hostmap rules). If they can't provide, ask for a repro in a controlled host where they can temporarily bypass the proxy (eg tether phone or alt network) to prove it works without proxy.

maria: customer did rapid test: bypassing proxy -> calls succeed immediately. So it's confirmed proxy. They asked if Redwood has any headers they can check to detect interception (we don't control proxy behavior but you can detect via cert chain and SNI mismatch). Recommended check: on client, run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -showcerts` and verify subjectCN and chain.

julie: also file these notes into support KB: "Proxy interception causes TLS name mismatch / CONNECT target rewrite" with reproducible steps and tcpdump examples. We'll also add an automated repro checklist for Support to request: pcap, curl -v, proxy vendor/config, whether app uses embedded truststore.

maria: closing loop with customer: provided temporary workaround (allowlist our egress IPs) and action items for customer security team: 1) configure proxy to tunnel for api.redwood.ai 2) OR add corporate CA to client truststores where acceptable. They were happy to escalate to network team. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: Note: file incident if recurring >3 customers in same org/ASN.

alex: if they later provide a pcap with modified CONNECT but still TLS for api.redwood.ai open a runtime ticket (eng-runtime) — there are a handful of appliances that rewrite CONNECT target based on hostmap and we may want to add guidance for Private deployments to use static IPs or prefix-based allowlists.

maria: thanks team. I'll update KB and ping product/docs to include recommended proxy rules for Private/VPC customers.

julie: thanks — adding to docs backlog. :white_check_mark:
